qs.ans: Flour per roti = 1/4 ÷ 12 = 1/48 kg (1 mark); 6 × 1/48 = 1/8 kg (1 mark).

qs.q: A tap fills 7/10 of a tank in 1 hour. What part fills in 2/3 hour? How long does it take to fill the full tank?
qs.ans: 2/3 × 7/10 = 14/30 = 7/15 of the tank (1½ marks). Full tank: 1 ÷ 7/10 = 10/7 = 1 3/7 hours (1½ marks).

qs.q: Mira's novel has 400 pages. She read 1/5 of the pages yesterday and 3/10 today. How many pages are left?
qs.ans: Yesterday 1/5 × 400 = 80 (1 mark); today 3/10 × 400 = 120 (1 mark); left 400 − 200 = 200 pages (1 mark).

Using a unit square, show and find 3/4 × 2/5. Explain the steps, and state the general rule.
qs.ans: Shade 2/5 of the square (2 of 5 rows) (1 mark). Divide it into 4 equal parts by 4 columns: 5 × 4 = 20 cells, one part = 2/20 (1 mark). Take 3 parts: 6/20 (1 mark) = 3/10 (1 mark). Rule: a/b × c/d = (a×c)/(b×d) (1 mark).

qs.q: Which is heavier: 12/15 of 500 g or 3/20 of 4 kg? Show working.
qs.ans: 12/15 × 500 = 400 g (1 mark); 3/20 × 4000 g = 600 g (1 mark); so 3/20 of 4 kg is heavier (1 mark).

qs.q: Four fountains fill a cistern: the first in 1 day, the second in 1/2 day, the third in 1/4 day and the fourth in 1/5 day. (a) How many times does each fill the cistern in a day? (b) If they flow together, in how much time is the cistern filled? (c) Express this time in hours.
qs.ans: (a) 1 ÷ 1 = 1, 1 ÷ 1/2 = 2, 1 ÷ 1/4 = 4, 1 ÷ 1/5 = 5 (2 marks). (b) Together 1 + 2 + 4 + 5 = 12 times a day (1 mark), so time = 1/12 day (1 mark). (c) 1/12 × 24 = 2 hours (1 mark).

qs.q: Explain, with examples, when the product of two numbers is (i) greater than both, (ii) less than both, (iii) between the two.
qs.ans: (i) Both numbers greater than 1: 4/3 × 4 = 16/3, greater than both (1½ marks). (ii) Both between 0 and 1: 3/4 × 2/5 = 3/10, less than both (1½ marks). (iii) One between 0 and 1 and one greater than 1: 3/4 × 5 = 15/4, less than 5 and greater than 3/4 (1½ marks). Reason: multiplying by a number less than 1 takes a part; by a number greater than 1 takes more than the whole (½ mark).

State Brahmagupta's rule for dividing fractions. Use it to evaluate 2/3 ÷ 3/5 and check your answer by multiplication.
qs.ans: Rule: a/b ÷ c/d = a/b × d/c = (a×d)/(b×c) — multiply the dividend by the reciprocal of the divisor (2 marks). 2/3 ÷ 3/5 = 2/3 × 5/3 = 10/9 (2 marks). Check: 3/5 × 10/9 = 30/45 = 2/3 ✓ (1 mark).

qs.ans: 15/4 × 48/5 (1 mark); cancel 15 with 5 and 48 with 4: 3 × 12 (1 mark) = 36 sq ft (1 mark).

qs.q: Līlāvatī's 'Dramma-tic donation': a miser gave 1/5 of 1/16 of 1/4 of 1/2 of 2/3 of 3/4 of a dramma. 1 dramma = 1280 cowries. (a) Write the product. (b) Simplify it. (c) How many cowries were given? (d) What is the joke?
qs.ans: (a) 1/2 × 2/3 × 3/4 × 1/5 × 1/16 × 1/4 (1 mark). (b) = 6/7680 (1 mark) = 1/1280 dramma (1 mark). (c) 1/1280 × 1280 = 1 cowrie (1 mark). (d) The miser gave the least valuable coin, a single cowrie (1 mark).

qs.q: Evaluate (1 − 1/2) × (1 − 1/3) × … × (1 − 1/10). Make a general statement and explain it.
qs.ans: Each bracket 1 − 1/k = (k − 1)/k (1 mark). Product = 1/2 × 2/3 × 3/4 × … × 9/10 (1 mark). Numerators cancel earlier denominators (1 mark), leaving 1/10 (1 mark). In general (1 − 1/2) × … × (1 − 1/n) = 1/n (1 mark).

Fig. 8.4 type problem: a square of area 1 square unit; its top-right quarter is a smaller square; the triangle inside it is half the small square; the shaded part is 3/4 of the triangle. Find the shaded fraction, showing each multiplication.
qs.ans: Small square = 1/4 (1 mark). Triangle = 1/2 × 1/4 = 1/8 (2 marks). Shaded = 3/4 × 1/8 (1 mark) = 3/32 of the square (1 mark).
